title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Elect Obj. 1 Solut close: Eternal will admits no succession in the willer
pass_a_gloss: For, as Albert teaches, in those things which act through essence, the agent always holds himself in one way: He is not said Agent now and not before, except insofar as the act now is, and was not before. Nor do we think in God’s will itself a new or temporal act when we posit that, faith arriving, he becomes actually reconciled to this or that human to whom before faith he was only reconciliable: because God does not then begin to will that this believer be actually reconciled to him, who before faith conceived was reconciliable, but from all eternity he willed that at this very moment he both would be believing and actually reconciled. In the willer therefore there are not successive mutations, but in the thing willed, and those according to one eternal and most constant will of God.
pass_b_english: As Albert teaches, in things that act through essence the agent always holds himself in one way: he is not called “agent now and not before,” except insofar as the act now is and was not before. Nor do we invent a new or temporal act in God’s will itself when we say that, once faith has come, he becomes actually reconciled to this or that human being to whom, before faith, he was only reconciliable. God does not then begin to will that this believer should be actually reconciled to him—after having been only reconciliable before faith was conceived. From all eternity he willed that at this very moment the person both would believe and would be actually reconciled. Succession of changes is not in the willer, then, but in the thing willed—and those changes follow one eternal and most constant will of God.
source_text: Nam, ut docet Albertus, in illis quae agunt per essentiam, agens uno modo semper se habet: Non dicitur Agens nunc, & non prius, nisi quatenus actum nunc est, & non prius. Neque in ipsa Dei voluntate cogitamus novum aut temporaneum actum, quando ponimus fide adveniente illum fieri actu reconciliatum huic aut illi homini, cui ante fidem fuit tantum reconciliabilis: quia Deus non tunc incipit velle ut hic credens sit ei actualiter reconciliatus, qui fuit ante conceptam fidem reconciliabilis, sed ab omni aeternitate voluit ut hoc ipso momento & credens esset, & actu reconciliatus. In volente igitur non sunt mutationes succedaneae, sed in volito, eaedemque secundum unam, aeternam ac constantissimam Dei voluntatem.
